Subject: Initial evidence + call request for DPA/SCCs/UK Addendum

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked promising. Legal is asking us to start collecting evidence for an upcoming engagement. Could you send the latest DPA draft, a current subprocessor list, and any note on how Redwood is relying on SCCs/UK IDTA for cross-border flows?

We also want to schedule a short call (30 min) to scope a TIA/DTIA for our EU-hosted workloads and confirm whether an additional UK Addendum will be required for UK-resident data. Primary objectives for the call:
- Confirm legal basis and routing (SCCs vs. UK IDTA)
- Identify required evidence artifacts and owners
- Clarify subprocessors and any onshore/offshore routing exceptions

Attaching Legal Ops in case they want to join. Proposed times: 2027-04-03 09:00-11:00 BST or 2027-04-03 14:00-16:00 BST.

Can you confirm and share the artifacts ahead of the call?

Thanks,
Ben Hughes
Head of IT Ops
Acme Pharmaceuticals

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com

Cc: Legal Ops <legal.ops@acmepharma.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-01T11:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Initial evidence + call request for DPA/SCCs/UK Addendum

Hi Ben — great to hear from you and glad the demo was helpful.

We can cover that in a 30-min TIA scoping call. 2027-04-03 14:00 BST works for our team (we'll convert to local times). I attached a compact evidence pack to accelerate the discussion:
- redwood_dpa_draft_v2.pdf (current DPA text with redlines from our legal)
- subprocessor_list_20270401.csv (live export of subprocessors and regions)
- TIA_scoping_sheet.xlsx (initial scoping questions we use to size a DTIA)

High-level notes up-front:
- HOSTING: Your environment will be served from our EU region by default; we use SCCs for transfers from the EU to the US where applicable, and provide a UK Addendum where customers have UK-resident data.
- KEY SAAS CONTROLS: We include customer-segregated keys (optional via KMS), audit logs retention settings, and support for on-prem/closed VPC deployment for regulated workloads.
- TIMELINE: If we agree scope on the call, we typically deliver a TIA package within 10 business days (evidence + narrative) and can prioritize UK Addendum if requested.

Proposed agenda (30m):
1) quick intros (5m)
2) confirm account scope and where data originates (5m)
3) identify required artifacts and owners (10m)
4) next steps and timeline (10m)

I'll invite Marissa (privacy/DR) and Karthik (legal ops) to the call; Laura can help with subprocessor clarifications.

Are you able to share your must-have evidence items in advance (e.g., SOC 2 report, retention policy, approved subprocessor requirements)?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_dpa_draft_v2.pdf; subprocessor_list_20270401.csv; TIA_scoping_sheet.xlsx

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-01T12:10:00-04:00
Subject: Internal: Acme TIA prep + ownership

Marissa/Karthik/Laura — looped to align before the call with Acme (Ben Hughes). Call scheduled 2027-04-03 14:00 BST. A few quick asks so we present a crisp scope: 
- Marissa: review the DPA redlines I attached and flag any UK-specific addendum points we should surface (e.g., UK-specific data residency commitments, export controls language).
- Karthik: confirm whether we should propose SCCs + UK Addendum by default or present both as options. Also flag any contract escalation thresholds if Acme requests on-prem or dedicated capacity.
- Laura: please review the subprocessor CSV and confirm which subprocessors process personal data for the EU region and whether any of them are located in the UK.

Target: create a one-page transfer-scorecard with: primary flows, legal basis, subprocessors involved, outstanding artifacts, and estimated delivery dates. I'll draft during the call and we can finalize post-call.

Thanks — Jordan

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-02T09:48:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme TIA prep + ownership

Thanks Jordan — quick review notes on DPA and transfer posture: 
- DPA: redline looks good overall. Add clause clarifying fallback to UK Addendum when UK-resident data is in scope (we've had buyers explicitly require the addendum be incorporated by reference).
- SCCs vs UK IDTA: For customers with EU controllers and UK operations, we should present SCCs as the transfer mechanism for EU-origin data; separately offer the UK Addendum as contractual language that mirrors SCC protections for UK-origin data.
- Evidence: pull SOC 2 cert (last audit 2026-11), encryption-at-rest statement, key management doc. I'll pull those into a small evidence pack.
- Subprocessors: flagged two entries in the CSV that require follow-up: "FastCache Ltd" (edge caching in EMEA) and "LogRiver" (log aggregation — note they have a US shard). Laura, can you confirm whether LogRiver processes raw identifiers?

I'll prepare the transfer-scorecard template (CSV) and populate the initial rows before the call.

-marissa

See you on the call.

Ben
